topic: AI data-center power constraints and investable value capture
capture_method: curator-frozen extracts plus unadjusted market observations

extracts: The IEA estimated data-center, AI, and crypto electricity consumption could more than double from 460 TWh in 2022 to over 1,000 TWh in 2026.
The forecast is global and scenario-dependent; it does not identify which listed company can deliver incremental power at an attractive valuation.
Constellation announced a 20-year Microsoft PPA supporting restart of the 835 MW Crane Clean Energy Center.
The restart targeted 2028 and required NRC approval plus state and local permits; Constellation expected about $1.6 billion of restart investment.
This is contracted customer credit with delivery risk, not immediately deliverable MW.
FERC rejected without prejudice an amended PJM interconnection agreement increasing co-located load from 300 MW to 480 MW.
The order demonstrates that behind-the-meter power availability can face tariff, reliability, allocation, and regulatory barriers.
TeraWulf announced long-term leases to deliver more than 70 MW of data-center infrastructure for Core42/G42 operations.
The company still carried bitcoin-mining, customer, buildout, financing, power-cost, and execution risks; contracted MW is not the same as commissioned revenue-producing MW.
